items.prompt: State what is meant by compression.
items.canonical_answer: Compression reduces the size of a file, so that it takes less storage space and takes less time to transmit.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - reducing a file’s size, so storage space and transmission time both benefit.

items.prompt: Explain why a website compresses the photographs it publishes.
items.canonical_answer: Each compressed photograph takes less storage space on the site’s servers, and a smaller file takes less time to transmit to a visitor’s browser, so pages appear sooner. The connection’s speed is set by the connection and does not change; the saving is in the time, because fewer bytes carry the same picture.
marking_guidance: Reason: compressed photographs need less space on the servers - 1 mark.
Purpose: so each page takes less time to transmit, because the connection’s speed does not change and the saving comes from the smaller file - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 1.3 claim ledger.
objective_titles: Show understanding of the need for and examples of the use of compression

items.prompt: A clinic keeps scanned patient records and sends them between its branches. Explain why compressing the records saves the clinic money.
items.canonical_answer: Compressed records take less storage space, so the clinic pays for less of it, and when records are sent between branches a smaller file takes less time to transmit, so staff spend less time waiting. The connection’s speed does not change; the saving comes from fewer bytes carrying the same content, which is why the storage bills and the waiting both fall.
marking_guidance: Context: this clinic’s stored and sent records - 1 mark.
Reason: because the compressed files take less space and less transmission time, the money spent on storage falls - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Describe two situations in which compressing files is worthwhile.
items.canonical_answer: Storage is one: an archive of thousands of photographs takes far less disk space once each file is compressed, so the same hardware holds more. Transmission is the other: a smaller file takes less time to transmit to each recipient, so a download that once kept a whole class waiting now finishes while the register is being called.
marking_guidance: Features: two situations as two points, 1 mark each - the storage saving and the transmission-time saving, each with the reason it matters.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 1.3 claim ledger.
objective_titles: Show understanding of the need for and examples of the use of compression

items.prompt: Explain one benefit of storing a school’s marks spreadsheet with lossless compression.
items.canonical_answer: Every mark must come back exactly as it was stored, and lossless compression rebuilds the original file exactly, so the marks are safe while the file is smaller. The smaller file takes less storage space and less time to transmit when the marks are sent on, which means the school gains the size benefits without risking a single value.
marking_guidance: Benefit: the original file is rebuilt exactly, so no mark can change - 1 mark.
Because the file is smaller, storage and transmission are cheaper, so the exactness costs nothing - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 1.3 claim ledger.
objective_titles: Show understanding of lossy and lossless compression and justify the use of a method in a given situation

items.prompt: Explain one limitation of lossy compression for a photograph kept as the only record of an event.
items.canonical_answer: The detail lossy compression discards is removed permanently, so the rebuilt photograph is not exactly the one taken: fine texture and edges are coarser for good. A copy that later needs enlarging or printing cannot regain what was removed, so an uncompressed or lossless original should be kept separately, which is the limitation of relying on the lossy copy alone.
marking_guidance: Drawback: discarded detail cannot be recovered, so the file is a close copy, not the original - 1 mark.
Because enlargement and printing expose the missing detail, an original-quality copy must be kept too, so the lossy file cannot stand alone - 1 mark.

items.prompt: A school website will publish a recording of its choir and also hosts its written policies, which must be preserved word for word. Explain which compression method should be used for each, and why.
items.canonical_answer: The recording suits lossy compression: what the ear is least sensitive to can be discarded without listeners noticing, and the file becomes much smaller, so listeners on slow connections are not left waiting; the notes do not need to be restored exactly to be enjoyed. The policies need lossless compression: every word of a document that must be preserved exactly has to come back as filed, and lossless rebuilds the original file exactly, so no wording can shift. Each choice in this situation follows from what the file is for.
marking_guidance: Suitable choices named for both files - 1 mark for the recording as lossy, because discarded detail passes unnoticed by the ear.
Reason for the policies: lossless rebuilds the file exactly, so the words are preserved - 1 mark.
Context: the justification is developed in this scenario - enjoyment versus preservation is what decides it - 1 mark.

items.prompt: A charity sends photographs from its field projects to donors on slow rural connections. Explain how compressing the photographs helps the charity, and which method suits the photographs.
items.canonical_answer: Each compressed photograph is smaller, so donors on slow rural connections spend less time waiting for each picture to arrive, because fewer bytes travel for the same view while the connection’s speed does not change. Photographs suit lossy compression, because the eye is tolerant of discarded fine detail, so the files shrink further than lossless methods would take them and the pictures still look right.
marking_guidance: Context: this charity’s photographs on the given slow connections - 1 mark.
Reason: lossy suits photographs because the eye tolerates the discarded detail, so the smaller files mean less waiting time - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Asked to name a method of lossy compression, a learner writes 'the quality gets worse and the file gets smaller'. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: The learner has described the effect of lossy compression, not a method. A method says what the compression does to the data, for example discarding detail the eye or the ear is least sensitive to, whereas an effect says what the result looks or sounds like. The test: does the answer say what is done to the data? Then it is a method.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the error named - an effect of the compression has been given where a method was asked for, a confusion of the two.
1 mark: the correction with the test - a method states what is done to the data, such as discarding detail the eye or ear is least sensitive to.

items.prompt: State what is meant by calling a compression method lossless.
items.canonical_answer: A lossless method is one from which the original file can be rebuilt exactly after compression.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - the original file can be rebuilt exactly from the compressed file.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 1.3 claim ledger.
objective_titles: Show understanding of lossy and lossless compression and justify the use of a method in a given situation

items.prompt: Describe two features that distinguish lossy from lossless compression.
items.canonical_answer: Lossy permanently removes some of the data, so the original cannot be rebuilt exactly, whereas lossless records the same data in fewer bits and rebuilds the original exactly. Lossy typically reaches much smaller files for photographs and sound, because the discarded detail passes unnoticed, whereas lossless is the only safe choice where every character or number matters, such as text and spreadsheets.
marking_guidance: Features: two distinguishing points, 1 mark each - the exactness of the rebuild, and the size reach of each kind with the file types each suits.

items.prompt: Explain why a text file of an exam paper must not be compressed with a lossy method.
items.canonical_answer: Every character of the paper carries meaning, and lossy compression discards data permanently, so characters or spacing could change and the rebuilt file would not match the original. Lossless compression makes the file smaller while rebuilding it exactly, so the need for exact wording is what rules the method out and the safer one in.
marking_guidance: Reason: lossy discards data permanently, so wording could change - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the paper is compressed losslessly instead, because every character must return exactly - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Describe the difference between lossy and lossless compression.
items.canonical_answer: Lossy discards some of the data permanently, so the original file cannot be rebuilt exactly from the compressed one. Lossless rewrites the same data in fewer bits, so the original can be rebuilt exactly. Lossy suits photographs and sound, where discarded detail passes unnoticed, whereas lossless suits text and data files, where every value must return.
marking_guidance: Difference: the original is lost versus rebuilt exactly - 1 mark for the rebuild contrast, 1 mark for the file types each suits, whereas both sides are needed.

items.prompt: State what is meant by run-length encoding.
items.canonical_answer: Run-length encoding is a lossless compression method that replaces a run of repeated items with the item and the length of the run.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - a repeated run stored as the item plus the run’s length.

items.prompt: Explain why run-length encoding compresses a flat logo bitmap well but a photograph poorly.
items.canonical_answer: A flat logo has long runs of same-coloured pixels, and each run collapses into one colour-and-count pair, so the file shrinks a great deal. A photograph’s neighbouring pixels usually differ, so runs are short and there are many of them, and the pairs can take more space than the pixel codes they replace, which is why RLE suits flat images and not busy ones.
marking_guidance: Reason: the logo’s long runs each become one pair - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the photograph needs a different method, because its runs are short and the pairs multiply - 1 mark.

objective_titles: Show understanding of how a text file, bitmap image, vector graphic and sound file can be compressed

items.prompt: A school banner is a bitmap of wide flat stripes of colour. Explain how run-length encoding reduces the banner file’s size.
items.canonical_answer: Each stripe is a long run of same-coloured pixels, and run-length encoding replaces each run with one pair, the colour and the count, instead of storing a code for every pixel. A stripe of 300 identical pixels collapses into one pair, so the file holds a handful of pairs where it held thousands of pixel codes, which is the saving.
marking_guidance: Context: this banner’s flat stripes - 1 mark.
Reason: because each long run of one colour becomes a single colour-and-count pair, the file stores pairs instead of a code per pixel, so it shrinks - 1 mark.

items.prompt: Describe two ways in which different file types can be compressed.
items.canonical_answer: A bitmap with flat regions compresses losslessly with run-length encoding, which replaces runs of same-coloured pixels with colour-and-count pairs. A photograph or a music track compresses with a lossy method that discards detail the eye or the ear is least sensitive to, which shrinks the file much further while the picture or the sound still passes for the original. A vector graphic, already stored as a short list of drawing objects, compresses little and usually travels as it is.
marking_guidance: Features: two ways as two points, 1 mark each - RLE on flat bitmaps with its colour-and-count pairs, and lossy methods on photographs and sound with the detail they discard.

items.prompt:
A community radio station in Otavi records a half-hour programme each week. The programme has three parts: the recorded audio, a text script of the announcer’s words, and photographs of the guests.
(a) Identify which of the three parts can suitably be compressed with a lossy method, and which must use lossless. [2]
(b) Explain why the script must be compressed losslessly, referring to what would happen with a lossy method. [3]
(c) The station sends the finished programme to partner stations over a slow rural link. Explain how compressing the audio helps the station, referring to the time the transmission takes. [3]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) The audio and the photographs can suitably be compressed with a lossy method; the script must use lossless.
(b) Every word of the script carries meaning, and lossy compression discards data permanently, so words or spacing could change and the rebuilt script would not match the original. Lossless compression rebuilds the file exactly, so the wording is safe while the file is smaller.
(c) Compressed audio is smaller, so it takes less time to transmit over the slow rural link, because fewer bytes carry the same programme. The link’s speed does not change; the saving is in the time taken, which means partner stations receive the programme sooner and the station pays for less data.
marking_guidance: Part (a): identify the audio and photographs as lossy-suitable and the script as lossless - 2 points, 1 per identification.
Part (b): the reason the script needs lossless - 3 points: every character matters, lossy discards permanently so wording could shift, and lossless rebuilds exactly.
Part (c): the context of the given slow link - 3 points: the smaller file takes less transmission time, the link’s speed does not change, and the programme arrives sooner for the partner stations.

items.prompt:
One row of a banner bitmap was compressed with run-length encoding. The table shows the stored pairs. Read the table and answer the questions.

| Pair | Colour | Run length |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 10 |
| 2 | 2 | 3 |
| 3 | 5 | 3 |

(b) State how many pixels the row holds. [1]
(c) The file stores each pair as 8 bits for the colour and 4 bits for the count, and the uncompressed row stores each pixel’s colour code as 8 bits. Calculate the bits the RLE form uses and the bits the pixel codes use, and state which is smaller. [3]
(d) Explain, with a reason, why the saving would be smaller if the same row came from a photograph. [2]
items.canonical_answer:
(b) The runs are 10, 3 and 3, so the row holds 16 pixels.
(c) The RLE form uses 3 x 12 = 36 bits; the pixel codes use 16 x 8 = 128 bits; the RLE form is smaller.
(d) A photograph’s neighbouring pixels usually differ, so the runs shorten and there are many more of them. Runs of length one cost a 12-bit pair each against an 8-bit code, so the saving shrinks and can turn into a loss, because the pairs take more space than the codes they replace.
marking_guidance: Read the given table: the run lengths sum to the pixel count - (b) 16 - 1 mark, and the answer shows the row reconstructed from the pairs.
Answer and values: (c) 36 bits against 128 bits, with the RLE form the smaller result - 3 marks, one per correct figure and the comparison.
Reason: (d) a photograph’s differing neighbours shorten the runs, because the pairs then multiply, so the table’s kind of saving depends on long same-coloured runs - 2 marks.

context.situation: An RLE table for one row of a banner bitmap.
